comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the whole change extends this skill: combinatorial testing for interaction defects, and the rule that a pass/fail checker is itself tested before its 0-found counts.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added references/combinatorial-testing.md (NIST SP 800-142), scripts/coverage-measure.mjs (t-way coverage share), the oracle rule in SKILL.md Step 6 with scripts/leak-check.mjs as the worked example, and the reference-table, ledger, and done-checklist rows.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the oracle rule is this skill applied to a checker: the thing that decides pass or fail must be proven able to fail, so each new script ships a discriminating test.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added test/coverage-measure.test.mjs and test/leak-check.test.mjs: a hand-picked grid measures short while a covering array measures full, and the checker catches the variant leak and ignores the substring; a no-op script flips the must-fail cases.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the two issue behaviors (an interaction defect is tested with a covering array; a 0-leaks claim needs a tested checker) are enumerated as scenarios, stored, logged, and run on the harness.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added two @audience:agent scenarios to features/evidence/claims-match-evidence.feature with step defs driving the real scripts; regenerated the datastore; appended the coverage log.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

architectural-decision-records.why: the decisions (ship machinery not docs-only; place the oracle rule in comprehensive-test-strategy; ship two small scripts) are recorded in the same change.
architectural-decision-records.what: added docs/adr/0095-combinatorial-testing-and-tested-oracles.md (context, considered options, decision, consequences with honest limits) and a CHANGELOG entry.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review ran on the diff before this receipt; it raised five fail-closed / honest-limits findings, all fixed, and the review is recorded in the arch-review log.
judge-arch.what: dispatched the four-questions review to a general-purpose subagent; fixed the coverage-key type collision, the unvalidated constraints, the unnamed leak-check limit, the silently-dropped secret, and the dangling cross-reference.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

pattern-selector.why: the design choice was made on purpose: two small single-purpose scripts and a documented rule, no new abstraction for a single use, matching the skill's existing check-test-shape.mjs.
pattern-selector.what: chose no new pattern: coverage-measure.mjs and leak-check.mjs are plain scripts, and the oracle rule is documented in the existing skill rather than a parallel framework.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

skeptical-audit.why: the oracle rule is the evidence discipline applied to a checker: a 0-found claim is refused without the checker's own passing tests, and the checker's limits are named rather than left implicit.
skeptical-audit.what: the SKILL.md oracle rule refuses a 0-found claim without evidence (the checker's tests), and the ADR and SKILL.md name leak-check.mjs's limits (embedded machine secrets, common-word and markup-split secrets).
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: offline tooling over local trusted text; no untrusted input, auth, session, credential storage, or network surface (leak-check detects secret exposure in a text string but does not itself handle credentials or untrusted network input).

arch-encode.why: the discipline is a documented skill rule plus two reference scripts, following the skill pattern, not a new nearest-scoped AGENTS.md/decisions.md arch-gate rule.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, storage, retention, migration, or backup is touched.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no running system, service boundary, data model, or scaling surface; two small CLI reference scripts and docs.

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature flag, or rollback of a running system.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, SLO, alert, or golden signal.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no interactive user-facing surface; the new docs follow house style but add no UI.
